lessons.title: Determining Harvest Maturity: Moisture and Seed Color
lessons.body: Sunflower is ready to harvest when the back of the flower head turns from green to yellow-brown and the seeds are plump with a moisture content of about 20-25%. At this stage, the seeds have reached physiological maturity but are still too wet for safe storage. If you wait too long, shattering and bird damage increase. In Africa, where many farmers grow open-pollinated varieties, checking seed color is key: seeds should be black or striped (depending on variety) and the white fluff at the base of the seed (the 'beard') should be dry and brown. A simple test: rub a few seeds between your fingers; the seed coat should slip off easily, revealing a firm white kernel. Another practical method is to cut the seed with a knife; the inside should be solid, not milky. For accurate moisture measurement, use a moisture meter if available, or the salt test: mix a sample of seeds with dry salt in a sealed jar, shake for 3 minutes, and if the salt sticks to the sides, moisture is above 20%. Harvest when moisture is between 15-20% for combine harvesting, or 12-14% for manual harvesting and immediate storage. In many African countries like Tanzania, Nigeria, and South Africa, sunflower is harvested from May to July in the southern hemisphere and October to December in the northern hemisphere. Delaying harvest after the head turns brown can lead to losses of up to 30% due to shattering. So, monitor your field daily as the heads turn downward. When the back of the head is brown and seeds are black, it's time to harvest.

lessons.title: Harvesting Methods: Manual and Mechanical
lessons.body: Manual harvesting is common among smallholder farmers in Africa. It involves cutting the sunflower heads with a sharp knife, sickle, or machete, leaving about 10-15 cm of stem attached. Workers then either thresh the seeds immediately by beating the heads with a stick or rubbing them over a wire mesh, or they dry the heads in the sun for a few days to loosen the seeds. A single person can harvest about 0.2 hectares per day manually. For larger fields, mechanical harvesting with a combine harvester is more efficient. A combine can harvest 4-8 hectares per day, depending on field size and conditions. However, combines require proper settings to minimize seed loss and damage. In Africa, contract harvesting services are available in countries like Zambia and South Africa, where farmers rent combines. When using a combine, ensure the field is level and free of obstacles. The machine cuts the heads, threshes, and separates the seeds in one pass. For manual harvesting, timing is critical: harvest early in the morning when dew is present to reduce shattering. After cutting, dry the heads on a tarpaulin or concrete floor for 3-5 days, turning them daily. Then thresh by beating with a stick or using a mechanical thresher. In some regions, farmers use a 'sunflower thresher' attachment for tractors. For both methods, avoid harvesting when seeds are too dry (below 10% moisture) as they crack easily, or too wet (above 25%) as they clog machinery. Always clean the harvester between fields to prevent mixing varieties. Post-harvest, store seeds in a cool, dry place. Proper harvesting method affects seed quality and yield: manual harvesting can result in 5-10% loss, while mechanical can be 2-5% if well-adjusted.

lessons.title: Combine Settings for Sunflower Harvest
lessons.body: Setting a combine for sunflower harvest is different from cereals because sunflower seeds are large, light, and easily damaged. The key adjustments are concave clearance, cylinder speed, fan speed, and sieve settings. Start with a concave clearance of 2-3 cm at the front and 1-2 cm at the rear. This allows the large seeds to pass through without cracking. Cylinder speed should be low, around 250-400 rpm, to thresh gently. Too high a speed will crack or dehull seeds, reducing quality. The fan speed should be set to medium, about 600-800 rpm, to blow away light chaff without blowing out seeds. Sieves: top sieve opening should be about 1.5-2 cm, and bottom sieve about 0.8-1.2 cm. These settings may need adjustment based on seed moisture and variety. If seeds are dry (below 12% moisture), reduce cylinder speed further to 200-300 rpm. If moist (above 18%), increase cylinder speed slightly to 400-500 rpm and reduce forward speed. Ground speed should be slow, 3-5 km/h, to allow the header to pick up heads without shattering. The header should be set to cut about 15-20 cm below the head, and the reel speed should match ground speed. In Africa, many farmers use older combines like the Claas Dominator or Massey Ferguson, which may need more frequent adjustments. Always check for seed loss behind the combine: if you see more than 2-3 seeds per square foot, adjust settings. Also, check the grain tank for cracked seeds; if more than 5% are cracked, reduce cylinder speed. After harvest, clean the combine thoroughly to prevent disease spread. Proper settings can reduce loss to 2-3% and maintain seed quality for oil extraction or planting.

lessons.title: Drying and Storage of Sunflower Seeds
lessons.body: After harvesting, sunflower seeds must be dried to a moisture content of 8-10% for safe storage. In Africa, sun drying is the most common method. Spread seeds in a thin layer (5-10 cm) on a clean tarpaulin, concrete floor, or woven mat. Stir the seeds every 2-3 hours to ensure even drying. Under full sun, seeds can dry from 20% to 10% moisture in 2-3 days. If the weather is cloudy, drying may take 5-7 days. For large quantities, use a mechanical dryer with a temperature not exceeding 43Â°C to avoid damaging the oil quality. Once dried, seeds should be cool before storage. Store in clean, dry jute bags or polypropylene sacks. Never use bags that previously held fertilizers or chemicals. Place bags on wooden pallets in a well-ventilated, dry room. Stack bags no more than 10 high to prevent crushing. Keep away from walls by 50 cm to allow air circulation. For long-term storage (more than 6 months), keep seeds in airtight containers or silos with moisture-proof liners. Add desiccants like silica gel if available. In humid regions, use hermetic storage bags like Purdue Improved Crop Storage (PICS) bags, which prevent moisture and insect damage. Check stored seeds monthly for signs of mold, insects, or heating. If temperature rises above 25Â°C, aerate the storage. Sunflower seeds are susceptible to insects like the red flour beetle and Indian meal moth. Use approved insecticides like Actellic dust at 1-2 kg per tonne, or natural methods like neem leaves. Proper drying and storage can maintain seed quality for up to 12 months. Poor storage leads to aflatoxin contamination, which is a health risk. Always test moisture before storage: bite a seed; it should crack, not be soft.

lessons.title: Quality Grading and Standards
lessons.body: Quality grading of sunflower seeds is based on moisture content, foreign matter, damaged seeds, and oil content. In Africa, standards vary by country but often follow regional or international norms. For example, the East African Community (EAC) standard for sunflower seeds requires moisture â¤10%, foreign matter â¤2%, broken seeds â¤3%, and oil content â¥40% for oilseed grade. In Nigeria, NAFDAC and SON set similar standards. Grading is done visually and with simple tools. First, take a representative sample of 1 kg from each lot. Spread it on a clean surface and remove foreign matter like stones, sticks, and other crop seeds. Weigh the foreign matter; if it exceeds 2%, clean the lot. Next, check for damaged seeds: cracked, insect-damaged, or discolored seeds. Count them; if more than 5%, the lot is downgraded. Moisture is measured with a moisture meter; if not available, use the salt test or oven method. Oil content is tested in labs, but farmers can estimate by pressing a small sample. Grades: Grade 1 (premium) has â¤1% foreign matter, â¤2% damaged, moisture â¤9%, oil â¥45%; Grade 2 (standard) has â¤2% foreign matter, â¤5% damaged, moisture â¤10%, oil â¥40%; Grade 3 (substandard) has >2% foreign matter, >5% damaged, moisture >10%, oil <40%. For seed production, germination rate must be â¥85%. In markets, higher grades fetch better prices. For example, in Tanzania, Grade 1 sunflower seeds sell for 20-30% more than Grade 3. To improve grade, clean seeds with a sieve or winnowing, dry properly, and store in clean bags. Always label bags with grade, moisture, and date. Selling ungraded seeds often results in lower prices and rejection by processors. So, invest time in grading to maximize returns.

lessons.title: Post-Harvest Loss Prevention
lessons.body: Post-harvest losses in sunflower can be 10-30% if not managed well. Major causes include shattering during harvest, poor drying, insect pests, rodents, and mold. To prevent losses, start at harvest: harvest at the right maturity to avoid shattering. Use tarpaulins under plants when cutting heads to catch fallen seeds. After harvest, dry seeds properly to 8-10% moisture; mold grows above 12% moisture. Store in airtight containers or hermetic bags to prevent insects. For rodent control, keep storage areas clean, use traps, or keep cats. For insects, use approved pesticides or natural repellents like neem. Regularly inspect stored seeds; if you see webbing or live insects, re-dry or fumigate. In Africa, the larger grain borer (Prostephanus truncatus) is a major pest of stored seeds; it can cause up to 40% loss. Use hermetic storage like PICS bags to control it without chemicals. Also, avoid mixing old and new seeds; old seeds may carry pests. For transport, use clean, dry bags and avoid overloading to prevent tearing. During storage, keep bags off the floor on pallets and away from walls. Control humidity by ventilating the store on dry days. If using a warehouse, ensure it is bird-proof and rat-proof. For long-term storage, consider silos with aeration. Another loss is from birds in the field; use bird scarers like reflective tape or noise makers. In some regions, farmers lose seeds to theft; secure your store. Finally, keep records of harvest and storage to identify loss points. By following these practices, you can reduce losses to less than 5%. Remember, every seed saved is money in your pocket. Proper post-harvest handling is as important as good agronomy.

quiz.q: What is the ideal moisture content for sunflower seeds at harvest for combine harvesting?
quiz.explanation: Combine harvesting is best when seed moisture is between 15-20% to minimize damage.

quiz.q: Which part of the sunflower plant turns from green to yellow-brown to indicate maturity?
options: C) Back of the flower head
quiz.explanation: The back of the flower head changes color as seeds mature.

quiz.q: What is a simple field test to check if sunflower seeds are ready for harvest?
options: A) Shake the head to hear seeds rattle
B) Rub seeds between fingers; seed coat slips off easily
C) Taste the seed for sweetness
quiz.explanation: When seeds are mature, the seed coat slips off easily, revealing a firm white kernel.

quiz.q: How many hectares can a person harvest manually per day?
quiz.explanation: Manual harvesting is labor-intensive, averaging about 0.2 hectares per person per day.

quiz.q: What is a recommended cylinder speed for a combine harvesting sunflower?
quiz.explanation: Low cylinder speed (250-400 rpm) prevents seed cracking and dehulling.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid harvesting sunflower when moisture is below 10%?
options: C) Seeds stick to the head
quiz.explanation: Very dry seeds are brittle and crack during threshing, reducing quality.

quiz.q: What is the maximum recommended temperature for mechanical drying of sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: Temperatures above 43Â°C can damage oil quality and seed viability.

quiz.q: Which storage method is best for preventing insect damage in sunflower seeds?
options: B) Hermetic storage bags like PICS
quiz.explanation: Hermetic bags create an airtight environment that kills insects without chemicals.

quiz.q: What is the recommended moisture content for safe storage of sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: Moisture below 10% prevents mold and insect growth during storage.

quiz.q: Which pest is a major cause of storage losses in sunflower in Africa?
quiz.explanation: The larger grain borer (Prostephanus truncatus) can cause up to 40% loss in stored seeds.

quiz.q: What is the maximum allowed foreign matter for Grade 1 sunflower seeds according to EAC standards?
quiz.explanation: Grade 1 premium seeds have â¤1% foreign matter.

quiz.q: How can a farmer estimate oil content without a lab?
options: A) By pressing a small sample
D) By counting seeds per head
quiz.explanation: Pressing a small sample can give a rough estimate of oil content.

quiz.q: What is a common method to prevent bird damage in sunflower fields?
quiz.explanation: Reflective tape or noise makers scare birds away.

quiz.q: Why is it important to clean a combine between fields?
quiz.explanation: Cleaning prevents mixing varieties and spreading diseases.

quiz.q: What is the recommended stack height for sunflower seed bags in storage?
options: A) No more than 10 bags high
quiz.explanation: Stacking more than 10 bags high can crush seeds in lower bags.

quiz.q: Which of these is a sign of poor quality sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: High percentage of damaged seeds downgrades the lot.

quiz.q: What is the salt test used for?
quiz.explanation: The salt test is a simple field method to estimate seed moisture.

quiz.q: When is the best time of day to harvest sunflower manually to reduce shattering?
options: B) Early morning when dew is present
quiz.explanation: Harvesting in early morning when dew is present reduces shattering.

quiz.q: What is the recommended concave clearance for a combine harvesting sunflower?
quiz.explanation: This clearance allows large seeds to pass without cracking.

quiz.q: How often should you stir seeds during sun drying?
quiz.explanation: Stirring every 2-3 hours ensures even drying and prevents mold.

quiz.q: What is the minimum germination rate for seed-grade sunflower?
quiz.explanation: Seed-grade sunflower must have at least 85% germination.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a cause of post-harvest loss in sunflower?
quiz.explanation: Proper drying prevents loss; it is not a cause.

quiz.q: What is the recommended moisture content for manual harvesting and immediate storage?
quiz.explanation: For manual harvesting and immediate storage, seeds should be 12-14% moisture.

quiz.q: How can you prevent mold growth in stored sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: Mold grows when moisture is above 12%; keeping below 10% prevents it.

quiz.q: What is the first step in quality grading of sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: A representative sample is essential for accurate grading.

quiz.q: Which grade of sunflower seeds fetches the highest price?
quiz.explanation: Grade 1 premium seeds have the highest quality and price.

quiz.q: What is a common natural method to control insects in stored sunflower seeds?
quiz.explanation: Neem leaves are a natural insect repellent.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using bags that previously held fertilizers for storing sunflower seeds?
options: A) They may contain chemicals that contaminate seeds
quiz.explanation: Chemical residues can contaminate seeds and affect quality.

quiz.q: What is the recommended ground speed for a combine harvesting sunflower?
quiz.explanation: Slow ground speed (3-5 km/h) allows proper picking and reduces shattering.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of using hermetic storage bags like PICS?
options: B) They control insects without chemicals
C) They are easy to carry
quiz.explanation: Hermetic bags create an airtight environment that kills insects naturally.
